page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance engineered on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is driven by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 silicon operating at 2.8 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated physical cores with single-thread allocation per core. The processor architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache pool. Complementing the processing cores is 64 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Storage performance is centered on an integrated 5,000 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by an 8 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark assessments show distinctive strengths in memory subsystems and local data handling. PassMark memory testing registers in the top 10 percent, supported by uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 189.45 GB/s, placing it in the top quartile of tested instances. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also achieves upper-tier performance at 14.41 GB/s. Standard integer and floating-point computations via Geekbench (multi-core score of 10,135) and multi-core stress-ng tests reflect median capabilities. Conversely, cryptographic throughput in PassMark and lower-tier small model LLM inference speeds highlight architectural bounds where advanced x86 vector or dedicated matrix instruction sets are absent.

The hardware configuration provides favorable resource efficiency for scenarios requiring massive local IOPS and high RAM capacity without incurring the overhead of attached network volumes or auxiliary GPU silicon. The integration of 5,000 GB of direct-attached NVMe storage paired with top-tier memory bandwidth suits transactional databases, Elasticsearch clusters, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, and high-throughput logging pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.2xlarge is a storage-optimized virtual instance powered by 8 dedicated AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. Featuring a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it supplies 64 GB of RAM alongside an integrated 5,000 GB local NVMe SSD and an 8 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark profiles reveal exceptional memory performance, highlighted by top-tier PassMark memory scores and strong uncached read bandwidth reaching 189.45 GB/s. While general multi-core compute scores remain in the median range and cryptographic tests reveal architecture-specific constraints, the large local solid-state storage and memory density provide effective efficiency for intensive storage pipelines. The instance is suited for distributed data storage, transactional databases, search indexing, and real-time streaming analytics.
